findings.description: This bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, unlike aws_s3_bucket.audit_trail, so objects such as the seeded vendor-roster.xlsx are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key and rely on whatever account/BucketKey default applies. Data at rest is not protected by an explicit, auditable encryption control.

The bucket holding ledger exports has no server_side_encryption_configuration block and therefore no customer-managed encryption key. Financial ledger data is stored unencrypted by any explicit control.

Versioning and logging are enabled but no server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without an explicitly configured key. Logging to the audit bucket does not substitute for encryption of the object data itself.
This bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbook contents without an explicit encryption-at-rest control or customer-managed key.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached and the bucket does not even set an explicit private ACL, so there is no bucket-level guardrail preventing a later policy or ACL change from exposing the bucket publicly.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached to this bucket. Defence in depth against accidental public exposure depends solely on the private ACL with no block-public-access guardrail.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached to this bucket, so the public-access guardrail that suppresses public ACLs and policies is not enforced at the bucket level.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached to this bucket, leaving no bucket-level enforcement that public access remain blocked.

The audit-trail bucket uses a log-delivery-write ACL (as required to be a logging target) but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so the grant-based ACL model is not constrained by a block-public-access guardrail on this security-sensitive bucket.
